name: Object.keys()
description: Returns an array of a given object's own enumerable property names, in the same order as a for...in loop.
parameters: obj — the object whose keys are to be returned.
returns: An array of strings representing the object's own enumerable keys.
notes: Does not include inherited or non-enumerable properties.

name: Object.values()
description: Returns an array of a given object's own enumerable property values.
parameters: obj — the object whose values are to be returned.
returns: An array of the object's own enumerable values, in the same order as Object.keys().

name: Object.entries()
description: Returns an array of a given object's own enumerable [key, value] pairs.
returns: An array of [key, value] pair arrays.
notes: Commonly paired with destructuring in a for...of loop: for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(obj))

name: Object.assign()
description: Copies all enumerable own properties from one or more source objects to a target object, mutating and returning the target.
parameters: target — object to copy properties into. sources — one or more objects to copy properties from.
notes: Performs a shallow copy — nested objects are still shared by reference. Passing {} as target avoids mutating a source object.

name: Object.freeze()
description: Freezes an object, preventing new properties from being added and existing ones from being removed or changed.
returns: The same object that was passed in, now frozen.
example: const o = Object.freeze({ a: 1 }); o.a = 2; // fails silently (throws in strict mode)
notes: Freezing is shallow — nested objects inside a frozen object are not themselves frozen.

name: Object.isFrozen()
description: Determines whether an object is frozen, meaning it is non-extensible and all its properties are non-configurable and non-writable.
returns: true if the object is frozen, otherwise false.

name: Object.create()
description: Creates a new object using an existing object as the prototype of the newly created object.
parameters: proto — the object to use as the new object's prototype. propertiesObject — optional property descriptors.
returns: A new object with the specified prototype.
example: const proto = { greet() { return 'hi'; } }; const o = Object.create(proto); o.greet(); // 'hi'
notes: Object.create(null) creates an object with no prototype at all, useful as a plain dictionary.

name: Object.getPrototypeOf()
description: Returns the prototype (internal [[Prototype]]) of the specified object.
parameters: obj — the object whose prototype to return.
returns: The object's prototype, or null if it has none.

name: Object.setPrototypeOf()
description: Sets the prototype of a specified object to another object or null.
parameters: obj — the object to modify. prototype — the new prototype (an object or null).
notes: Changing the prototype after creation is slow — prefer Object.create() when possible.

name: hasOwnProperty()
description: Returns a boolean indicating whether the object has the specified property as its own (not inherited).
parameters: prop — the property name (string or symbol) to test.
returns: true if the object directly owns the property, otherwise false.
notes: The safer Object.hasOwn(obj, prop) is now preferred since it works even on objects created with Object.create(null).

name: Object.defineProperty()
description: Defines a new property directly on an object, or modifies an existing one, with fine-grained control via a descriptor.
parameters: obj — target object. prop — property name. descriptor — object describing value, writable, enumerable, configurable, or getter/setter.
returns: The object that was passed to the function.
notes: Properties defined this way are non-enumerable by default, so they won't show up in Object.keys() or for...in.

name: Object.fromEntries()
description: Transforms a list of key-value pairs into an object, the inverse of Object.entries().
parameters: iterable — an iterable such as an array of [key, value] pairs, or a Map.
returns: A new object built from the entries.
notes: Handy for converting a Map back into a plain object, or for transforming entries with map()/filter() before rebuilding.

name: Object.seal()
description: Seals an object, preventing new properties from being added but allowing existing writable properties to be changed.
returns: The same object that was passed in, now sealed.
example: const o = Object.seal({ a: 1 }); o.a = 2; // allowed; o.b = 3; // ignored
notes: Less restrictive than Object.freeze() — existing property values can still be reassigned.

name: Object.is()
description: Determines whether two values are the same value, using stricter semantics than === for edge cases like NaN and signed zero.
parameters: value1, value2 — the two values to compare.
returns: true if the values are the same value, otherwise false.
example: Object.is(NaN, NaN); // true — unlike NaN === NaN which is false
notes: Object.is(0, -0) returns false, whereas 0 === -0 returns true.

name: Object.getOwnPropertyNames()
description: Returns an array of all own property names of an object, including non-enumerable ones but excluding symbol keys.
parameters: obj — the object whose property names to return.
returns: An array of strings representing all own property names.
notes: Unlike Object.keys(), this also includes non-enumerable properties.
